name: Spinnable AI employees
operator: Spinnable (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Spinnable's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Role-based AI workers with their own email address, memory, scheduled tasks and access to 35+ connected tools, reachable by email, WhatsApp, Slack, meetings and voice.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Part of the first Portuguese cohort.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: Autonomy 3 rests on I08 and I17, so I17 carries the level. The only evidence is one sentence in the troubleshooting page, under a heading for missing context or ambiguous instructions: the worker may pause and wait for manager guidance rather than guessing. The words are hedged (may), the page presents it as a failure case with a fix (give the missing information or write fallback instructions in the Worker Policy), and it is not a stated design in which routine work is done by the worker and exceptions go to a person. The source says what the note says, and grade documented and mode default are right, but it is weak support for the indicator. Without I17 the card has no Autonomy level at all (I18 and I19 are not answered, and Autonomy 2 needs I16, or I07 with one of I02 to I05, none of which is answered), so the whole card turns on this sentence. Suggest the assessor look for a firmer page (for example the Worker Policy or the automation settings page, or the paused-task email in I40 as a defined exception path) or record that the level rests on one hedged sentence.

The note says the security guide advises that recipients of a company-address worker need not know. No such statement is in the corporate-email page cited, and the scan lists no security guide among its sources; I grepped all fetched Spinnable pages for it and found nothing. The rest is correct: the corporate-email page says outbound email includes a default disclosure footer reading 'is an AI worker hired through Spinnable', that managers can turn the Email signature setting off, and that turning it off removes the footer. Remove the unsourced clause or add and capture the source. Span is in the page and under fifteen words (the scan uses the placeholder form from the page). Mode default is right since the signature is on by default. It feeds Openness only through any(I56, I22, I58), which I22 and I58 already satisfy, so no level changes.

Span 'When a worker delegates tasks to other workers in your team' is in the 10 June 2026 release note (Sub-Tasks Activity Trail); mode available with configuration multi-worker is right because it needs two or more workers. The sentence 'Since 13 May 2026 a worker can also be added as co-manager of another worker' is not on the cited page: it comes from the docs llms.txt index entry for 13 May 2026, which reads 'Workers as co-managers'. Cite that source in the note or drop the sentence. The page does not itself say that workers have their own context and authority, though the AI workers page says each has its own email address (I26), so the scope fit is acceptable. I12 feeds only Autonomy 4, which the card does not reach.

Release note of 5 August 2026 says Read means workers can search and look up but never create, change or send; Full access 'stays the default'; and 'When you connect a new account, Read is preselected'. The page is therefore internally mixed on which is the default. Mode available (configuration read-only-connection) is the conservative and right reading. Span is in the source. I25 is not used by any level on this card (Reach 3 also needs a published agent interface; Control 2 needs I38, which is not answered).

Span 'Only the worker's manager or co-managers can change these controls' is in the communication-restrictions page (differs from the scan text only in the apostrophe). The page does document a per-worker setting for who may message the worker. The indicator is 'A limit on it is a setting that its own account could change' (lens: barrier of the kind setting); the evidence shows a setting that managers change, which fits the lens reading but not clearly the 'its own account' wording. It feeds no level. Consider noting the reading used.

Connecting-tools page says 'All tool actions are logged with' timestamp, worker ID, tool and method used, success or failure status, and user context. Note matches. Indicator needs operation and the grade is documented, so it correctly counts for nothing; Control 3 would need I41, I39 and I43 with observed or measured evidence. Control stays 1 on I47 (Worker Policy, 'highest-priority rules', a rule in prose). Control 1 therefore rests on a prose rule, a modest basis, but the span is exact and the rule matches I47.

Home page testimonial by the CEO of Smart Role says Clara manages his calendar, runs his outreach and keeps his pipeline current, and that two workers were running in under an hour; the span is exact. It names a customer for work the workers do, so it meets the 'names a customer' branch of S1; it gives no sessions, tasks or pull requests. It is a quote chosen and published by the vendor, which the note already says. S1 earns the badge only and feeds no level.

Checked in the fetched pages. I04: vault page says credentials are exposed as VAULT_ environment variables to Python code in the code execution sandbox, mode default fits. I08: AI workers page says they can check a calendar, update databases and send emails. I10 and I11: tools overview lists many tools by category (HubSpot, Salesforce, GitHub, Notion, Google tools) and authentication by OAuth 2.0 or API key. I20: introduction. I21: tool-permissions page, tools granted per worker with a chosen connection. I22: troubleshooting page documents a worker that stops mid-way, with causes and fixes. I26: 'They have their own email addresses'. I30: change-manager page says 'A worker's manager can administer its settings'. I39: communication-channels page says interrupt cancels the current in-flight generation; the 28 October note covers pausing failing recurring tasks. I40: 28 October release note says a recurring task failing or blocked three runs in a row is paused and the manager emailed with the reason. I47: Worker Policy passage. I57: support page gives an email channel for worker issues, for managers and for workers. I58: privacy policy lists email content, calendar events, documents, messages and customer data from integrated platforms. I68: docs llms.txt lists dated release notes through 28 October 2026. S3: an llms.txt resolves on both www.spinnable.ai and docs.spinnable.ai (observed, fetched). Spans in the scan that my checker flagged as not found (I30, I40, I46) differ from the page only by curly versus straight apostrophes, so they pass. All spans are under fifteen words. Grades and modes are fine; no needs operation answer is counted as documented for a level. S4 is not answered and no agent-callable interface was seen in the sources, which is consistent with Reach 2.

Card computed as A3, R2, C1, O2. Level 3 appears only in Autonomy (I08 plus I17, see the I17 finding); nothing is at level 4. Reach 2 rests on I10 and I11, both documented connectors lists, an artefact. Openness 2 rests on I22 and I58, both public pages (troubleshooting and privacy policy), artefacts and not adjectives. Control 1 rests on one prose rule (I47). The I54 answer the assessment lowered is not on the card and no source I read contradicts that.

Re-sourced to the home page; the span 'takes initiative, scheduling tasks, sending follow-ups, flagging issues, and completing workflows' is exact (11 words) and in the page's FAQ answer to 'How autonomous are the workers?', which opens with 'Very.' The span covers only the routine half of the indicator. The exceptions half ('a person approves key actions' in the note) is not in the span: it comes from other parts of the same page ('Approve key actions' beside a UI mockup, and 'it won't take actions with external consequences without your approval. When it's unsure, it asks instead of improvising'). I searched the docs pages in the scan (introduction, ai-workers, tool-permissions, troubleshooting) and found no documented approval mechanism, so the person-handles-exceptions half rests on marketing copy and a mockup. Autonomy 3 turns on this one answer: remove I17 and the card has no Autonomy level. Round one's finding is partly answered (firmer than a hedged troubleshooting sentence, but still one vendor marketing paragraph). Fix: quote a span that carries the exception half, for example the 'asks instead of improvising' sentence, or add a docs page that describes approvals, and say in the note that no docs page describes how approval is configured.

New, minor. The note says a person can interrupt a running worker, which the communication-channels page supports ('This immediately cancels the current in-flight generation'), and adds 'failing recurring tasks are paused'. That second clause is from the 28 October release note (the I40 source), not the cited page. It is in a source of the scan, so the rule is met, but the note should name the release note. Interrupt is a stop of one reply, not a stop of the worker; the indicator is met only loosely. No level effect.

The docs llms.txt lists dated notes from 8 January to 28 October 2026 at mostly weekly intervals but with gaps (for example 24 June to 8 July, 29 April to 13 May, none between 22 January and 5 February). Say 'dated release notes, most weeks'. The span 'October 28, 2026' is exact and appears in the index. No level effect.

New, minor. The span 'Vault environment variables exist solely inside the sandbox code execution environment.' is exact, but it states a restriction on where keys are visible and not that the worker generates and runs code; the code execution claim is in the note and in the vault page's table ('Exposed as VAULT_ environment variables for Python code and custom scripts'). A span from that table row would fit the indicator better. No level effect (I04 is not used on this card).

Card computed as A3 R2 C1 O2; nothing at level 4. Arguing against Autonomy 3 (the only level three): it rests on I08 and I17. I08 is a documentation statement that workers update databases and send emails (artefact, fine). I17 is one FAQ answer on the home page that begins 'Very.' (an adjective in the source, not credited) and a mockup, with no docs page describing approvals or exception handling; the 'person handles exceptions' half of the level is the note's reading of marketing text. If I17 is removed the card has no Autonomy level (I15, I16 and I07 with I02 to I05 are not answered), so the weakest fact removes a whole dimension. Mode default is honest if approvals are on by default, but no source says that. Autonomy 4 would need I18 or I19 and is correctly not claimed. Against the weakest credited levels elsewhere: Control 1 rests on I47 only (a Worker Policy of 'highest-priority rules'), modest but exact; I41 and I39 exist as documented but I41 is needs operation, so Control 3 is correctly withheld; Control 2 lacks I38. Reach 2 rests on I10 and I11 (a connector list, an artefact); Reach 3 needs a published agent interface, none seen. Openness 2 rests on I22 (troubleshooting page) and I58 (privacy policy), both artefacts. Fix for the card is the I17 span and note above.

I04.n: Workers run Python code and custom scripts in a sandbox, where stored credentials are exposed as environment variables.
I04.span: Exposed as VAULT_ environment variables for Python code and custom scripts

I08.n: The documentation states workers act in connected tools, such as updating databases and sending emails.
I08.span: They can check your calendar, update databases, and send emails.

I10.n: Workers connect to many tools across a business, from email and calendar to GitHub, Notion and Salesforce.
I10.span: connect to 35+ tools to work across your entire tech stack

I11.n: Each tool is connected by authenticating with the outside service through OAuth or an API key.
I11.span: Authenticate with the service (OAuth or API key)

I12.n: With two or more workers in a team, a worker can delegate tasks to the others; each sub-task shows as its own block in the activity trail (release notes, 10 June 2026).
I12.span: When a worker delegates tasks to other workers in your team

I17.n: The home page FAQ states that a worker schedules tasks, sends follow-ups and completes workflows without being prompted each time, that it will not take actions with external consequences without the person's approval and asks when unsure; no documentation page describes how that approval is configured.
I17.span: it won't take actions with external consequences without your approval

I20.n: The documentation states what the workers are for: joining a team and doing its work, by role or for a specific process.
I20.span: AI workers that join your team and help you get work done.

I21.n: Tools must be granted to each worker separately, with a chosen connection and capabilities such as read or send.
I21.span: A connection under Settings > Tools does not grant any worker access by itself.

I22.n: The troubleshooting page documents failure cases, such as a worker stopping mid-workflow, with causes and fixes.
I22.span: Your worker initiates a task or multi-step workflow, but stops mid-way

I25.n: A tool connection can be set to Read, so the workers using it can look things up but not create, change or send; Read is preselected for a new connection, while Full access remains the default and is needed to act.
I25.span: When you connect a new account, Read is preselected

I26.n: Each worker has its own email address, separate from the people it works for.
I26.span: They have their own email addresses and can send/receive messages

I30.n: Each worker has a manager who administers its settings; the role can be handed to another user.
I30.span: A worker's manager can administer its settings

I39.n: A person can interrupt a worker from the chat with Send now, which cancels the reply it is generating; the page describes stopping a run, not stopping the worker as a whole.
I39.span: This immediately cancels the current in-flight generation

I40.n: A recurring task that fails three runs in a row is paused and the worker's manager is emailed with the reason.
I40.span: Spinnable pauses it and emails the worker's manager with the reason.

I41.n: The documentation states every tool action is logged with time, worker, tool, method and outcome; documented, not observed.
I41.span: All tool actions are logged with:

I46.n: Who may message a worker is a per-worker setting in the same workspace account that runs the worker, changed by its manager or co-managers; the page does not say the worker itself can change it.
I46.span: Only the worker's manager or co-managers can change these controls.

I47.n: Persistent rules for a worker are written in prose in its Worker Policy.
I47.span: Worker Policy instructions are treated as the highest-priority rules and apply across all conversations.

I56.n: By default, a worker's outbound email carries a signature footer saying it is an AI worker hired through Spinnable; a manager can switch the signature off, which removes the footer. Email only; no disclosure is documented for WhatsApp, Slack or voice.
I56.span: is an AI worker hired through Spinnable

I57.n: A support page gives an email channel for reporting problems with a worker, for managers and for workers themselves.
I57.span: How to get help when something goes wrong

I58.n: The privacy policy lists what the agents access: email, calendar, documents, messages and data from connected platforms.
I58.span: When our AI agents work for you, they access:

I68.n: The documentation index lists dated release notes from 8 January to 28 October 2026, most weeks, with some gaps.

S1.n: The home page quotes Smart Role's CEO: one worker manages his calendar, runs his outreach and keeps his pipeline current. A testimonial; no usage figures for what the workers do.
S1.span: Clara manages my calendar, runs my outreach, and keeps my pipeline current.

S3.n: An llms.txt resolves on the marketing site and on docs.spinnable.ai, fetched on 10 November 2026.
S3.span: AI Workforce Fit Guide for AI Agents

not_credited.what: AI disclosure for a worker that sends from a company email address
not_credited.why: The security best practices page says recipients of such a worker do not and should not know it is an AI; this qualifies the I56 footer, which applies to the default Spinnable signature only, and is recorded here rather than in the I56 note because it is a different source. Add this URL to the scan's sources and run tools/capture.mjs so it carries a hash.

not_credited.what: AI disclosure when the default email signature is off
not_credited.why: The corporate-email page, a captured source, says the disclosure footer is part of the Spinnable signature card and is not controlled separately. It says that turning off Email signature removes the footer, and its troubleshooting gives that as the fix when the footer appears on outgoing emails. No other disclosure is documented, so I56 is credited for the default only.

not_credited.what: A configured approval step for worker actions
not_credited.why: The home page says actions with external consequences need approval, but no captured documentation page describes an approval setting. The corporate-email page's troubleshooting says to 'Designate a single point of contact for send approvals and critical instructions' and to make this explicit in the Worker Policy, which is a prose rule and not a mechanism. Not credited as I38; I17 rests on the home page statement only.
